title: The Front-Loaded Mortgage Shock

beats.say: You buy a $400,000 home with a 30 year mortgage at 6.5%.
beats.visual: A cinematic macro shot of a single house key resting on a dark wooden table, warm low-key lighting, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: You think your monthly payments are chipping away at that debt.
beats.visual: A sleek dark fountain pen resting on blank white paper, moody side lighting, slow subtle camera push-in.

beats.say: Wait until you see where your money actually goes during the first five years.
beats.visual: A close-up of a vintage brass desk lamp casting a warm pool of light on an empty leather planner.

beats.say: Over 60 months, you hand the bank roughly $150,000 in total payments.
beats.visual: A blurred abstract shot of dark water ripples catching faint golden reflections from a distant streetlight.

beats.say: That sounds like massive progress on your massive loan.
beats.visual: An extreme close-up of dark coarse sand falling slowly through a metal funnel, moody cinematic light.
A stark minimalist concrete wall with a single sharp shadow cutting across the frame, overcast daylight.

beats.say: Because of how banks front-load the interest, almost all of it vanishes.
beats.visual: A dark, heavy metal gear turning slowly in half-shadow, industrial aesthetic, slow motion.

beats.say: After 5 years and $150,000 spent, you have only paid down $17,000 of principal.
beats.visual: A hand wearing a dark wool coat sleeve sliding a heavy metal slider on a dark mixing board, macro shot.

beats.say: The rest went straight to bank interest and escrow fees.
beats.visual: A dark brass pocket watch ticking in a patch of morning light, dust motes floating in the air.

beats.say: You didn't buy equity. You bought rented time.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person standing by a tall glass window looking out at a moody twilight city skyline.

beats.say: Know the rules of the debt before you sign the papers.
beats.visual: A stack of dark leather-bound books resting on a heavy oak desk, dramatic rim lighting from the side.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A clean cinematic shot of a dark hallway with a single glowing amber light at the far end.

caption: Most homeowners have no idea where their first five years of payments actually go. Check the math before you sign. #mortgagemath #personalfinance #moneyrules #debtfree #housingmarket
description: Analyzing a $400,000 30-year mortgage at 6.5% reveals the hidden reality of front-loaded interest. After paying $150,000 in 5 years, only $17,000 goes to principal.
first_comment: Did your mortgage amortization schedule shock you when you first looked at it?

facts.claim: A $400,000 30-year mortgage at 6.5% leaves only about $17,000 paid to principal after 5 years of payments totaling roughly $150,000
facts.basis: Standard standard loan amortization mathematics for a 30-year fixed mortgage at 6.5% interest on a $400,000 principal balance.
